headline: Mandya faces surge in child marriages and teenage pregnancies, raising concerns about maternal and child undernutrition risks.
summary: Mandya district, known as 'Sugar Town', has seen a troubling rise in child marriages with 147 complaints received, 62 cases registered, and 85 prevented in 11 months of 2023. Among pregnant minors identified, 43 are below 18 years, including three aged 15, ten aged 16, and thirty aged 17. The District Administration has constituted a committee to check child marriages. While stunting prevalence among school children in rural B. G. Nagara area has been studied, specific recent district-wide undernutrition data is limited. Pregnant women in rural areas face anaemia challenges, and Anganwadi food quality issues affect child nutrition programmes.

reasons.detail: Anaemia screening identified as important for pregnant women in rural Mysore area, as untreated anaemia leads to maternal and foetal complications.
Children refusing Anganwadi meals, with discontent replicated across several Anganwadis, undermining nutrition programme effectiveness.
Health concerns about minors getting pregnant, with mandatory reporting by healthcare providers bringing more cases to light.
